January, 2015

Author: H.C.Mishra
Bench: H.C.Mishra
 In The High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi
 W.P. (Cr.) No. 159 of 2014
 -------
 Sunil Agarwal @ Sunil Kr. Agrawal .... Petitioner

Coram : Hon'Ble Mr. Justice H.C.Mishra
For the Petitioner : : M/s. Dilip Kr. Prasad

For the Respondents : : M/s. S.C.-II  -------
07/ 23.01.2015 Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned counsel for the State.

2. This writ application has been filed by the petitioner with a prayer for quashing the exparte  order dated 25.12.2013 passed by the Deputy Commissioner, RanchicumAdjudicating  Officer, respondent No.2, in Food Safety & Standards Case No. 28/2013 14, whereby the penalty of Rs.3,00,000/ lakhs has been imposed upon the petitioner,

as  the sample of Noodles purchased from the shop of the petitioner was found to be misbranded.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner has taken a short point in challenging  the impugned order, submitting that the said order has been passed exparte  without service of notice upon the petitioner.

The ordersheet has been brought  on record, which shows that the complaint under the Act was filed by the Food  Safety Officer, Ranchi, on 20.4.2013 in the Court of the Deputy Commissioner, 
Ranchi, which was registered as Food Safety and Standards Case No. 28/ 2013 14.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Case No. 28/ 2013
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: On 20.4.2013 itself, notice was ordered to be issued to the accused person  and the case was fixed for 29.5.2013.
There is nothing in the ordersheet to  show that the notice was actually issued to the accused person.

On the next  date fixed, i.e., on 29.5.2013 the case could not be taken up as the Deputy Commissioner was busy  w i t h t h e o t h e r w o r k s a n d t h e c a s e w a s f i x e d f o r  28.06.2013, on which date also for the same reason the case was not taken up  Sunil Agarwal vs The State Of Jharkhand And Ors on 23 January, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132447748/
1 and the case was fixed on 07.08.2013.

entities.text: Sunil Agarwal vs The State Of Jharkhand And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On 07.08.2013, the State was heard and  the case was fixed for orders and finally the impugned order dated 25.12.2013  was passed imposing the penalty upon the petitioner, and in the said order it is  mentioned that upon proper notice the accused did not appear and hence the matter was taken ex parte against him.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the impugned  order passed by the Court below cannot be sustained in the eyes of law, in as  much as, no notice was ever issued / served to the petitioner and it has falsely  been stated in the impugned order that upon proper notice, the accused did not appear.
2  5.

The same stand has been taken by the petitioner in paragraph8 of the writ application, 
w h e r e i n i t i s s t a t e d t h a t t h e l e a r n e d F o o d S a f e t y O f f i c e r , 
Ranchi, filed an application for adjudication before the Deputy Commissioner, 
who without service of notice as well as compliance of other provision, passed the order dated  2 5 . 1 2 . 2 0 1 3 .

I t i s s u b m i t t e d b y l e a r n e d c o u n s e l f o r t h e  petitioner that even though the counteraffidavit has been filed by the State, 
but there is no reply to this statement in the writ application. 
6 . L e a r n e d c o u n s e l f o r t h e S t a t e o n t h e o t h e r h a n d h a s o p p o s e d t h e p r a y e r  and has pointed out from the impugned order itself, that it is mentioned therein  that proper notice was served to the accused and in spite of that the accused  did not appear and hence the matter was taken up exparte.
It is submitted by learned counsel  f o r t h e S t a t e t h a t a c c o r d i n g l y , t h e r e i s n o i l l e g a l i t y i n t h e  impugned order passed by the Deputy Commissioner, Ranchi.

7. As regards to the reply to the statement made in paragraph8 to the writ  application, it is only stated in paragraph22 of the counteraffidavit filed on  behalf of the State, as follows: "22 That with regard to the statement made by the  petitioner in paragraph7 to 10, in the instant writ petition under reply, it is humbly  stated and submitted that the same are matter of record hence required no comment." 
8.

After having heard learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned  counsel for the State, as also upon going through the record, I find that it is  apparent that there is no specific denial by the respondentState that the notice was never served  upon the petitioner.

The ordersheet in Food Safety & Standards Case No. 28/2013 1 4 o n l y s h o w s t h a t b y o r d e r d a t e d 2 0 . 0 4 . 2 0 1 3  there was only an order of issuance of notice to the accused person.
There is nothing in the order s h e e t t o s h o w t h a t t h e n o t i c e w a s a c t u a l l y i s s u e d t o t h e  opposite party
and on the subsequent two dates the case could not be taken up  by the Deputy Commissioner, Ranchi, as he was only busy with other works.

On the third  consecutive date, the State was heard and the case was fixed for  Sunil Agarwal vs The State Of Jharkhand And Ors on 23 January, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132447748/
2 orders and finally, the impugned order dated 25.12.2013 was passed, imposing  the penalty upon the petitioner and mentioning that upon proper notice the  accused did not appear and hence the matter was taken exparte against him.

entities.text: Sunil Agarwal vs The State Of Jharkhand And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This statement in  t h e i m p u g n e d o r d e r e x f a c i e s h o w s t h a t i t i s a g a i n s t t h e  record and the notice was actually never issued / served upon the petitioner  before passing the order of penalty by the impugned order dated 25.12.2013.

Indeed, the order sheet clearly shows that the case was never even fixed for ex parte hearing, before the State was heard on 7.8.2013.
3 9 . I n m y c o n s i d e r e d v i e w , t h e i m p u g n e d o r d e r d a t e d 2 5 . 1 2 . 2 0 1 3 p a s s e d b y  the respondent No.2, is absolutely illegal, having been passed without affording  any opportunity to the petitioner to defend himself, and the same cannot be  sustained in the eyes of law.

10. Accordingly, the impugned order dated 25.12.2013 passed by the learned Deputy  Commissioner, RanchicumAdjudicating Officer, in Food Safety & Standards Case No. 
28/201314, is hereby, quashed.
This application is accordingly, allowed.

(H.C.Mishra, J.) D.S.
